step1_figure.description: Figure 24.33 shows an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with an NMOS differential input pair (M1, M2), PMOS current mirror loads (M31/M3, M41/M4), NMOS current mirror (M51/M5), and tail current source M6. Figure 24.34 on page 798 shows the open-loop AC test configuration with large resistor (100 MEG) and capacitor feedback for DC stability driving a 1 pF load.

open_loop_dc_gain.description: Low-frequency small-signal differential open-loop voltage gain

equation.explanation: With mirror ratio K = 1, the small-signal gain is given by the input transconductance multiplied by the parallel output resistance of PMOS mirror transistor M4 and NMOS mirror transistor M5.
equation.assumptions: Quiescent bias current per diff branch ~ 10 uA, K = 1, load impedance is predominantly capacitive at high frequencies

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming Iss = 20 uA (Id1 = Id2 = 10 uA), with typical (W/L)n = 25, g_mn = sqrt(2 * un*Cox * (W/L) * Id) = sqrt(2 * 270u * 25 * 10u) = 367 uA/V. Output resistance ro4 = ro5 = 1 / (lambda * Id) = 1 / (0.1 * 10u) = 1 MOhm. ro4 || ro5 = 500 kOhm. A_v = 367 uS * 500 kOhm = 183.5 V/V = 45.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: In SKY130 at 1.8V, channel length modulation and finite output resistance yield low-frequency gains typically in the range of 30 to 48 dB.

equation.explanation: The effective short-circuit output transconductance equals the input differential transconductance scaled by mirror ratio K.
equation.assumptions: Output shorted to AC ground, K = 1

sky130_expected.calculation: With K = 1 and Id = 10 uA, gm_OTA = g_mn = sqrt(2 * 270u * 25 * 10u) = 367 uA/V (0.367 mA/V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on input pair transistor sizing and tail current bias point.

equation.explanation: Frequency where the open-loop gain drops to 0 dB (unity gain) when driving a capacitive load CL.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker obtained 24 MHz with standard Table 9.2 params (150 uA/V gm); in SKY130 with 25 W/L, gm ~ 350-400 uA/V yields 40-70 MHz.

equation.explanation: 3-dB roll-off frequency set by the output node resistance and the load capacitor CL.
equation.assumptions: C_L = 1 pF, output node dominates bandwidth

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by r_o of output transistors and 1 pF external capacitance.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin at the unity-gain crossover frequency

equation.explanation: Phase difference from -180 degrees at the unity-gain frequency. A single high-impedance node OTA typically exhibits near single-pole response (~90 degrees PM).
equation.assumptions: Mirror poles (M3/M31, M5/M51) are located significantly beyond fun

sky130_expected.calculation: Single dominant pole gives -90 deg phase at high frequencies; parasitic mirror poles contribute ~5 to 15 deg phase lag at fun ~ 50 MHz. PM = 180 - (90 + 10) = 80 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Mirror nodes have low impedance (1/gm), placing non-dominant poles well above 100 MHz.

slew_rate.description: Large-signal slew rate when driving load capacitor CL

equation.explanation: Maximum output current available to charge or discharge CL is bounded by K * Iss, where Iss is tail bias current of M6.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Slewing is entirely limited by the tail current being steered to one side and mirrored to the output capacitor.

quiescent_power.description: Static DC power dissipation of the OTA core and bias network

equation.explanation: Total static DC power drawn from the 1.8V rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: Core current: tail M6 (20 uA) + M3/M51 branch (10 uA) + M4/M5 branch (10 uA) = 40 uA. Bias circuit draws ~ 60 uA. Total current ~ 100 uA. P_diss = 1.8 V * 100 uA = 180 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard biasing conditions in 180 nm / Sky130 technology at 1.8V supply.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for Baker OTA (Fig. 24.33 / Fig. 24.34) measuring DC operating point, power, open-loop gain, unity-gain frequency, 3-dB bandwidth, phase margin, transconductance, and transient slew rate.
